subject: math
title: Numbers to 100: Tens and Ones, Comparing and Skip Counting
seo_title: Grade 2 Numbers to 100 Math Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on numbers to 100: tens and ones with base ten blocks, the value of each digit, comparing and ordering, counting by 2s, 5s and 10s, the hundred chart and number lines. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 4 in 47 is worth 40.
key_sub: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones: 40 + 7. To compare, look at the tens first: 47 < 74.
body_html:
Tens and ones

10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. A 2-digit number has a tens place and a ones place.

The value of a digit

The place tells you what a digit is worth.

47 = 40 + 7. If a place is empty, write 0 there: seventy is 70.

Write the number

Write “sixty-three” as a number.

6 tens and 3 ones. Write the tens digit first: 6, 3.

Answer: 63 (not 36 or 603)

Compare and order

Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones.

Compare

47 ☐ 74

Tens: 4 tens < 7 tens.

Answer: 47 < 74

> means “is greater than”. < means “is less than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Count by 2s, 5s and 10s

Skip counting is fast counting. By 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. By 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. By 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40.

Hundred chart and number lines

On a hundred chart, one step right is 1 more. One step down is 10 more.

On a number line, find what each mark is worth before you count.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up the digits (47 and 74)Write the tens first, then the ones
Reading the digit, not its value (the 4 in 47 is 4)The 4 is in the tens place: 40
Counting blocks, not their values (4 rods and 7 cubes = 11)Count rods by 10s, then add the ones: 47
Writing each part you hear (sixty-three = 603)A number less than 100 has 2 digits: 63
Comparing the ones first (58 > 60)Compare the tens first: 60 > 58
Counting the marks on a number lineFind what each mark is worth, then count

faq.q: What number skills are in the Grade 2 BC math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 2 students in BC work with number concepts to 100: counting, skip counting by 2s, 5s and 10s, place value with tens and ones, and comparing and ordering numbers.

faq.q: How do I explain tens and ones to a Grade 2 child?
faq.a: Use base ten blocks or bundles of 10 straws: 10 ones make a ten. Then 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones, or 40 + 7.

faq.q: Why does my child write 74 for 47?
faq.a: Mixing up the digits is a common place value mistake. Ask how many tens and how many ones, and remind them that the tens digit is written first.

faq.q: How can children practise skip counting at home?
faq.a: Count pairs of socks by 2s, nickels by 5s and dimes by 10s. A hundred chart helps too: counting by 10s moves straight down a column.

sets.title: Tens and ones with base ten blocks

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 tens and 7 ones make 47. Write the tens digit first: 47, not 74.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 tens and 5 ones make 35. Count the rods by 10s: 10, 20, 30. Then count on 5: 35.

items.q: How many tens are there?
items.e: Each rod is 1 ten. There are 5 rods, so there are 5 tens. The number is 58.
A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 6 tens and 0 ones make 60. Count the rods by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. No cubes means 0 ones.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: There are 4 rods and 2 small cubes. That is 4 tens and 2 ones: 42.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 tens and 9 ones make 29. Count the rods by 10s: 10, 20. Then count on 9 ones: 29.

items.q: How many ones are there?
items.e: Each small cube is 1 one. There are 9 cubes, so there are 9 ones. The number is 39.

items.q: Which number has 6 tens and 3 ones?
items.e: Write the tens digit first, then the ones: 6, 3. That is 63.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 5 tens and 3 ones make 53. Count the rods by 10s to 50. Then count on 3: 51, 52, 53.

items.q: Add 1 more rod. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 36. A rod is 10. 36 + 10 = 46. Only the tens digit changes.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: There are 2 rods and 5 small cubes. That is 2 tens and 5 ones: 25.
A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 7 tens and 6 ones make 76. Count the rods by 10s to 70. Then count on 6 ones: 76.
There are no small cubes, so there are 0 ones. The number is 70.

items.q: Which number has 5 tens and 0 ones?
items.e: 5 tens is 50. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place: 50 (fifty, not fifteen).
A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 8 tens and 1 one make 81. 8 tens is eighty. 81 is eighty-one, not eighteen (18).

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: 14 small cubes are 1 ten and 4 ones. 3 tens + 1 ten = 4 tens. So the number is 44. Check: 30 + 14 = 44.
A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 9 tens and 4 ones make 94. Count the rods by 10s to 90. Then count on 4 ones: 94.

items.q: Add 1 more small cube. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 59. Add 1 cube: now there are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. That is 6 tens and 0 ones: 60.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 ten and 6 ones make 16. This is sixteen. Sixty-one (61) is 6 tens and 1 one.
Each rod is 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30 … 100. 10 tens make 1 hundred.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. The red 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 40. The digit is 4, but its value is 40.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: 74 is 7 tens and 4 ones. The red 4 is in the ones place, so it is worth 4.

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 62?
items.e: 62 is 6 tens and 2 ones. The 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: In 58, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 58 is 5 tens and 8 ones. The tens digit is 5. (Its value is 50.)

items.q: Write “sixteen” as a number.
items.e: Sixteen is 1 ten and 6 ones: 16. Sixty is 60. Listen for “teen”.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: 38 is 3 tens and 8 ones. The red 3 is in the tens place, so it is worth 30. The digit is 3, but its value is 30.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the tens place?
items.e: 62 is 6 tens and 2 ones. 26 and 16 have 6 ones, not 6 tens. 6 has no tens.

items.q: What is the value of the 3 in 83?
items.e: 83 is 8 tens and 3 ones. The 3 is in the ones place, so it is worth 3.

items.q: What is 47 in expanded form?
items.e: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. 4 tens = 40. So 47 = 40 + 7.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: 91 is 9 tens and 1 one. The red 9 is in the tens place, so it is worth 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: Write “seventy” as a number.
items.e: Seventy is 7 tens and 0 ones: 70. Seventeen is 17.

items.q: In 71, which digit is in the ones place?
items.e: 71 is 7 tens and 1 one. The ones digit is 1. It is the digit on the right.

items.q: Which number has a 3 in the ones place?
items.e: 43 is 4 tens and 3 ones. 34, 30 and 38 have 3 tens, not 3 ones.

items.q: What is the value of the 9 in 95?
items.e: 95 is 9 tens and 5 ones. The 9 is in the tens place, so it is worth 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: What number is 90 + 2?
items.e: 90 + 2 is 9 tens and 2 ones: 92. Do not write 90 and then 2. The answer has only 2 digits.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: 56 is 5 tens and 6 ones. The red 6 is in the ones place, so it is worth 6.

items.q: Write “eighty-five” as a number.
items.e: Eighty-five is 8 tens and 5 ones: 85. Do not write 80 and then 5. It has only 2 digits.

items.q: Which number has 0 ones?
items.e: 70 is 7 tens and 0 ones. 7 and 17 have 7 ones, and 71 has 1 one.

items.q: What is the value of the 2 in 25?
items.e: 25 is 2 tens and 5 ones. The 2 is in the tens place, so it is worth 20. The digit is 2, but its value is 20.

items.q: 100 = ☐ tens. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30 … 100. That is 10 tens. 10 tens make 1 hundred.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 7 tens is more than 4 tens. So 74 > 47.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 9 tens is more than 3 tens. So 93 > 39.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tens. 86 has 8 tens, the most. So 86 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare the tens. 13 has 1 ten. The others have 3 tens. So 13 is the least.

items.q: What number is 10 more than 36?
items.e: 10 more: add 1 ten. The tens digit goes from 3 to 4: 46. (37 is 1 more. 26 is 10 less.)

items.q: Which number is greater than 63?
items.e: 71 has 7 tens and 63 has 6 tens. So 71 > 63. The others are less than 63.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 6 tens is more than 5 tens. So 60 > 58. Do not compare the ones first: 8 ones is more than 0 ones, but 58 is less.

items.q: Put 47, 74 and 44 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 74 has 7 tens, so it is the greatest. 44 and 47 have 4 tens. Ones: 4 < 7, so 44 < 47. Order: 44, 47, 74.

items.q: Which number is between 40 and 50?
items.e: 46 has 4 tens, so it is between 40 and 50. 64 and 54 are too big. 39 is too small.

items.q: What number is 1 less than 70?
items.e: 1 less: count back 1. 70, 69. (60 is 10 less. 71 is 1 more.)

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 100 has 3 digits and 99 has only 2. So 100 > 99.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 97 and 90 both have 9 tens. Ones: 7 ones > 0 ones. So 97 is the greatest.

items.q: Put 29, 92 and 9 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 9 has only 1 digit, so it is the least. 29 has 2 tens and 92 has 9 tens. Order: 9, 29, 92.

items.q: Which number is less than 45?
items.e: 39 has 3 tens and 45 has 4 tens. So 39 < 45. The others are greater than 45.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 52 > 25.

items.q: What number is 10 less than 100?
items.e: 10 less: take away 1 ten. 10 tens − 1 ten = 9 tens = 90. (99 is 1 less.)

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 40, 45 and 44 have 4 tens. Ones: 0 is the fewest. So 40 is the least.

items.q: Which number is between 70 and 80?
items.e: 73 has 7 tens, so it is between 70 and 80. 37 and 67 are too small. 83 is too big.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 8 tens is more than 1 ten. So 81 > 18.

items.q: Put 65, 56 and 60 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 56 has 5 tens, so it is the least. 65 and 60 have 6 tens. Ones: 5 > 0, so 65 > 60. Order: 65, 60, 56.

items.q: What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, ☐
items.e: Count by 2s: add 2 each time. 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ☐
items.e: Count by 5s: add 5 each time. 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: What comes next? 10, 20, 30, 40, ☐
items.e: Count by 10s: add 10 each time. 40 + 10 = 50.

items.q: Count by 2s. How many dots are there?
items.e: There are 7 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.

items.q: What comes next? 35, 40, 45, ☐
items.e: Count by 5s: add 5 each time. 45 + 5 = 50.
There are 6 groups of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

items.q: What comes next? 1, 3, 5, 7, ☐
items.e: Count by 2s from 1: add 2 each time. 7 + 2 = 9.
A full ten frame has 10 dots. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.

items.q: You count by 2s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting by 2s from 0, every number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 46 ends in 6.

items.q: What comes next? 7, 17, 27, 37, ☐
items.e: Count by 10s from 7: add 1 ten each time. The ones digit stays 7. 37 + 10 = 47.

items.q: Count the nickels by 5s. How much money is it?
items.e: A nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s 8 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. That is 40¢.

items.q: What number is missing? 65, 70, 75, ☐, 85
What comes next? 50, 48, 46, 44, ☐
items.e: Count back by 2s: take away 2 each time. 44 − 2 = 42.

items.q: There are 9 pairs of mittens. Count by 2s. How many mittens are there?
items.e: A pair is 2. Count by 2s 9 times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18.

items.q: Count the dimes by 10s. How much money is it?
items.e: A dime is 10¢. Count by 10s 7 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. That is 70¢.

items.q: What comes next? 90, 80, 70, ☐
items.e: Count back by 10s: take away 10 each time. 70 − 10 = 60.

items.q: You count by 5s from 0. Which number do you not say?
items.e: Counting by 5s from 0, every number ends in 0 or 5: 25, 30, 35, 40. 32 ends in 2.

items.q: What comes next? 100, 95, 90, ☐
items.e: Count back by 5s: take away 5 each time. 90 − 5 = 85.

items.q: On a hundred chart, you count by 10s from 3. Which numbers do you colour?
items.e: Counting by 10s from 3, add 10 each time: 3, 13, 23, 33. The ones digit stays 3. On the chart, you move straight down the column.

items.q: You count by 5s from 5 to 50. How many numbers do you say?

sets.title: Hundred chart, number lines and word problems

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number is the ?
items.e: Each step right is 1 more. Each step down is 10 more. 35 is above the ?, so the ? is 35 + 10 = 45.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 50 there are 5 jumps, so each mark is 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20 … 70.

items.q: On a hundred chart, which number is just below 47?
items.e: One row down is 10 more. 47 + 10 = 57. (48 is just to the right. 37 is just above.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 1. Count on from 45: 46, 47. The arrow is at 47.

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number is the ?
items.e: Look up: 67 is above the ?. One step down is 10 more: 67 + 10 = 77.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 1. Start at 70 and count on 6 marks: 71, 72 … 76.

items.q: On a hundred chart, which number is just above 82?
items.e: One row up is 10 less. 82 − 10 = 72. (92 is just below.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 50 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10 … 35. (7 is the number of marks, not the number.)

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number is the ?
items.e: Look up: 24 is above the ?. 24 + 10 = 34. It is also 1 more than 33.

items.q: The arrow is halfway between 20 and 30. What number is it?
items.e: From 20 to 30 there are 10 small jumps. Halfway is 5 jumps: 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: Kai has 4 packs of 10 hockey cards and 6 single cards. How many cards does he have?
items.e: 4 packs of 10 = 40. 40 + 6 = 46. (4 tens and 6 ones.)

items.q: On a field trip to a salmon hatchery, Ava counts 63 salmon. Liam counts 36. Who counts more?
items.e: Compare the tens: 63 has 6 tens and 36 has 3 tens. 63 > 36, so Ava counts more.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Simran gives 7 toonies. A toonie is $2. How much money is that?
items.e: Count by 2s 7 times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. 7 toonies are $14.

items.q: On a BC Ferries boat, the cars park in 9 lanes. Each lane has 10 cars. How many cars are there?
items.e: Count by 10s 9 times: 10, 20 … 90. 9 tens = 90.

items.q: Hana’s mystery number is between 60 and 70. It has 4 ones. What is it?
items.e: Between 60 and 70 means 6 tens. Then 4 ones: 64.

items.q: Owen reads 47 pages. Zara reads 74 pages. Who reads more pages?
items.e: Compare the tens: 74 has 7 tens and 47 has 4 tens. 74 > 47, so Zara reads more.

items.q: Arjun has 9 nickels. A nickel is 5¢. How much money does he have?
items.e: Count by 5s 9 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. 9 nickels are 45¢.

items.q: 12 students put on skates at the rink. Each student wears 2 skates. How many skates is that?
items.e: Count by 2s 12 times: 2, 4, 6 … 22, 24. 12 students wear 24 skates.

items.q: Today is day 87 of school. What day of school will it be in 10 days?
items.e: 10 days later is 10 more. 87 + 10 = 97. Only the tens digit changes. (88 is 1 more.)

items.q: Leah writes seventy-four as 704. What should she write?
items.e: Seventy-four is 7 tens and 4 ones: 74. It has only 2 digits. Do not write 70 and then 4.
